A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same f-INE work and contain readable main text, figures, algorithms, tables and appendices. Retained content can be matched despite reformatting and appendix reordering.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original MNIST label-noise detection and Llama-3.1-8B/LIMA poisoning-attribution experiments, including variability analysis and a qualitative case study.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds CIFAR-10 results, mini-ImageNet attribution examples, and LLM sensitivity experiments.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, line 9, changes the primary SGD update's starting parameters from the auxiliary model's parameters to the primary model's own parameters. This corrects the written recurrence; the two-stage gradient-similarity and hypothesis-testing procedure otherwise remains unchanged.

E1.justification: V2 adds CIFAR-10 mislabeled-sample detection and mini-ImageNet image-attribution evaluation in Appendices C and D, extending coverage to natural images. MNIST and poisoned LIMA remain, while v1's brief FEMNIST accuracy report disappears.

E2.justification: The classification comparisons retain Influence Functions, TraceIn, TRAK and random selection, including their extension to CIFAR-10. LLM comparisons retain LESS and random selection. The sensitivity studies evaluate configurations of existing methods without introducing new comparators.

E3.justification: New evaluations use ResNet-18 for CIFAR-10 and ResNet-50 for mini-ImageNet. Section 4.4 introduces controlled comparisons of projection dimensions from 1024 to 8192 and randomly subsampled 60 or 80 checkpoints against the 100-checkpoint configuration. These add substantive evaluation settings; retained experiments' textual protocols are largely unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 retains the seed-variability analysis and LLM poisoning case study, while adding sensitivity studies for gradient projection dimension and checkpoint count (Section 4.4, Figures 9–10). Appendix D additionally examines whether image-attribution rankings select semantically coherent training examples.

E5.justification: Both versions already report three LLM training runs, standard-deviation error bars and coefficients of variation. The new CIFAR-10 means and variances extend the existing repeated-run dispersion reporting; no increase in runs for retained experiments or new statistical inference procedure is stated.

E6.justification: Appendix C adds CIFAR-10 results reporting average advantages of 10.21% over TRAK and 14.04% over Influence Functions, plus variance estimates. V2 also adds sensitivity curves and mini-ImageNet rankings, newly quantifies the retained MNIST near-tie with TraceIn as 0.05% better, and removes the 62% FEMNIST accuracy report. Original LLM findings are retained.

T1.justification: The influence definitions, composition and normality results, and supporting proofs are preserved, with v1 Appendix C becoming v2 Appendix B. Added closing sentences restate the existing Gaussian composition formula and uniform-convergence argument without introducing new mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and conclusion retain the hypothesis-testing/privacy connection, Gaussian influence, efficient single-run estimation, and robust data-cleaning and LLM-attribution claims. Additional experiments support these claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 explains degradation through information lost in smaller projections and potentially missed distribution tails with fewer checkpoints. Appendix D interprets low-ranked cross-class examples as harmful, while Appendix A acknowledges applications where valuation for a specific training run is desirable.

D1.justification: The code disclosure changes from an anonymous repository described as containing all code to a named GitHub repository described as preliminary in Appendix E. Hardware, LoRA, optimizer and training details largely carry over from v1 Appendix B. Repository availability cannot be verified from the PDFs alone.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds discussion of Data Banzhaf, LAVA and in-run Data Shapley, expanding positioning relative to robust and algorithm-independent valuation. Dataset references are added and Cadamuro et al. (2016) is removed. Most other bibliography changes update metadata for retained works.

P1.justification: Most existing prose is retained. V2 adds Section 4.4, moves the former Section 4.3.3 case study to Section 4.5, reorders the proof and implementation appendices, adds a reproducibility statement, and makes localized wording, affiliation and acknowledgment edits.

P2.justification: V2 substantially expands the visual presentation with two sensitivity figures, a CIFAR-10 recall plot and a mini-ImageNet gallery (Figures 9, 10, 12 and 13). The conference format reflows and resizes existing displays, and the original histogram is redrawn and relabeled as Figure 11. Table 1 is retained.

improvement.justification: CIFAR-10 validation and the sensitivity studies provide useful evidence missing from v1 about applicability beyond MNIST and dependence on computational choices. Related-work additions improve positioning. The gains are limited by sparse configuration details for the new ResNet experiments and Appendix E's unreconciled MobileNetV2 description.
